logline: A little fishing-boat model survives two simulated oceans, then faces the distance between an interesting harvest rule and a season people can actually plan.

cold_open.picture: Extreme close-up of a small boat hanging from a lifting sling. A deckhand-sized shadow falls across it. Pull back: it is a scale model suspended over a glass research basin, not a real boat leaving port. A visible SIMULATION plaque makes the reveal literal.

escalation.beat: The model settles into the basin. The September11th paper appears as a source plate on the basin wall. Introduce policy discovery: simulated seasons let a learned rule encounter consequences and change.

Below the waterline, repeated routes through the basin reveal a physical return path to the learning mechanism. A neighboring fixed guide rail identifies the predefined comparison. Everything remains a schematic, not a data plot.

First basin: CONSTANT RECRUITMENT. Separate labels and outcome placards report higher spawning biomass and large annual catch swings. A season-planning board stands outside the glass. It remains blank because no business outcome was measured.

A full stage change lifts the same model into a second basin marked STOCK-LINKED RECRUITMENT. This is a different experiment. Higher catch and lower spawning biomass appear relative to its comparison. No smooth-curve animation and no claim that catches became steadier.

The model reaches a real harbor slipway and stops at the lip while the camera descends to water level. The paper has demonstrated modeled differences. It has not demonstrated a workable season. A full-size boat and shore equipment establish the change in stakes.

turn.drawn: The sling lowers the model toward open harbor water, then rotates it back into its clearly labeled research basin. This is an earned continuation of testing, not a defeat. A model should stay a model until its results answer the real management questions.

button.last_line: What should a new pollock rule have to prove before it leaves the basin?
button.last_image: Match the opening macro: same model in its sling. Now a small NEXT TEST plate faces the viewer. The final motion is toward the basin, not an unsupported real launch. Cut to12.3s credits.

sight_gags.gag: A wave splashes the model, then the camera reveals a research-basin paddle scarcely larger than a spoon. The scale joke establishes simulation.
A tiny captain figurine reaches for a celebratory flag at the higher-biomass placard; the adjacent catch-swings placard unfolds and gently blocks the flag.
At the real quay, the model’s absurdly tiny life ring slips down a full-size mooring post. The scale mismatch carries the operational limit without a lecturing stop sign.

the_test.strongest_fair_case_against: Interesting differences between policies in simplified oceans may not help actual managers or fishing businesses. A model result cannot establish acceptable catch stability or practical superiority.
the_test.drawn_at_full_strength: Bring the model directly beside full-size season equipment. Hold the threshold long enough that viewers expect a launch. Present RESEARCH RESULT beside SEASON REQUIREMENTS with no green checkmark joining them. The model returns for comparison instead of receiving approval.

two_loops.payoff: At68s the separate stock-linked experiment reverses the biomass outcome. The first result is not a universal AI advantage.

retention_plan.padding_test: A90-second cut loses the distinct second experiment or the fully drawn real-world test. The second basin changes the conclusion; the harbor threshold tests practical usefulness instead of repeating simulation terminology. If time runs long, cut decorative travel and the third gag before cutting either argument.

stages: Glass simulation basin with visible drive and waterline
Separate second research basin with different geometry and explicit scenario label
Working harbor slipway with full-size vessel and shore equipment
production_constraints.representation: Schematic only. No numerical scales, fish-count masses, unlabeled curves or changing outcome heights. Use directional words beside separately named outcomes. No claim of actual autonomous boat use.
production_constraints.asset_feasibility: Boat, glass basin, sling, quay and mooring post can be built as simple layered vector props; requires motion/sound timing more than new illustrated panels.
